analysis: Examined the three changed files. ProviderLoop.swift (head 705-716, 868) adds state only: selectedModelRecovery, a test-only load override (nil in production), savedEnabledModels (seeded from config at init) and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. These add no network, crypto, or authorization surface. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift (head 50-51, 54) adds enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery to the DaemonState snapshot written by DaemonStateFile.write. The new fields carry model ID lists and a recovery status report. Model IDs are already exposed in advertisedModels, servingSelection and heartbeats, so there is no new prompt-derived or key material (A-001, A-003) and no change to the TB-011 authorization state (lastTrustStatus, clearConnectionAuthorization unchanged). ProviderLoop+Testing.swift (head 514-523) adds two test seams, setSelectedModelRecoveryLoadOverrideForTesting and awaitSelectedModelRecoveryAttemptForTesting. They are not gated with #if DEBUG, but they live in an internal extension and are described as test-only. The override is a stored property that is nil in production, and a local attacker cannot set it without code execution in the process (already covered by TB-003/T-013/T-014). The remaining test-seam code is unchanged context. Unverified, since the files are not in this batch: ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery (the selectedModelRecoveryReport implementation and the recovery load path, which is described as no-eviction) and the DaemonState struct definition and DaemonStateFile permissions. The next pass should confirm that selectedModelRecoveryReport emits no error strings containing paths or sensitive content, that the recovery load honours weight-hash verification (T-027/T-012), and that the state file stays owner-only. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.
